facts: **$V = Ah$**, where $A$ is the area of the uniform cross-section and $h$ is the perpendicular distance through the prism.
The "base" of a prism is its uniform cross-section, not necessarily the face it is sitting on.
Cross-section area formulas: rectangle $A = lw$, triangle $A = \frac{bh}{2}$, parallelogram $A = bh$, trapezium $A = \frac{h(a+b)}{2}$.
Every area formula uses the **perpendicular** height of the shape, never a slant side.
Put all dimensions in the same unit before substituting.
An area in cm² multiplied by a length in cm gives a volume in cm³.
steps: Find the area of the uniform cross-section.
Substitute the cross-section area and the perpendicular height into $V = Ah$.
Evaluate and write the answer in cubic units.

foundation.solution_text:
The perpendicular height of the triangle is $8$ cm; the $10$ cm side is a slant.
$V = Ah$
$= \left(\frac{6 \times 8}{2}\right) \times 5$
$= 24 \times 5$
$= 120\text{ cm}^{3}$

development.solution_text:
Prism A: $V = (5 \times 4) \times 8$
$= 160\text{ cm}^{3}$
Prism B: $V = \left(\frac{8 \times 5}{2}\right) \times 9$

$180 - 160 = 20$
Prism B is greater, by $20$ cm³.

mastery.question_text: A swimming pool is $25$ m long and $8$ m wide. The floor slopes evenly from $1$ m deep at the shallow end to $2.5$ m deep at the deep end, so the side wall of the pool is a trapezium. Find the volume of water in the full pool. Give your answer in m³.
mastery.solution_text:
The uniform cross-section is the trapezium-shaped side wall, and the width of the pool is the distance through it.
$A = \frac{25(1 + 2.5)}{2}$
$= 43.75\text{ m}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 43.75 \times 8$
$= 350\text{ m}^{3}$

mastery.question_text: A triangular prism has a volume of $96$ cm³. A new prism is made in which the base and the perpendicular height of the triangular cross-section are both doubled, and the length of the prism is halved. Find the volume of the new prism. Give your answer in cm³.
mastery.solution_text:
Doubling both the base and the perpendicular height multiplies the cross-section area by $2 \times 2 = 4$.
Halving the length multiplies the volume by $\frac{1}{2}$.
$V = 96 \times 4 \times \frac{1}{2}$
$= 192\text{ cm}^{3}$

Container A: $A = \frac{5(12 + 8)}{2}$
$= 50\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = 50 \times 15$
$= 750\text{ cm}^{3}$
Container B: $V = (10 \times 9) \times 8$
$= 720\text{ cm}^{3}$
$750 - 720 = 30$
Container A holds more, by $30$ cm³.
